credit_headline.narrative: Non-food bank credit grew 19.15% year-on-year in September 2026, the strongest reading in this 36-period series, bouncing back after August's brief easing from July's 19.1%. At the same time, all four main sectors — agriculture, industry, services and retail — stayed in positive YoY growth for a 27th straight period running back to July 2024. Together, the two readings show credit growth at its highest pace in this dataset while still spread across every major sector rather than concentrated in one.

sibc-bank-credit-abs.title: Bank credit hits ₹229.9L Cr — fresh high, up ₹6.1L Cr
sibc-bank-credit-abs.observation: Bank credit outstanding reached ₹229.9L Cr in September 2026, at or near the highest level in this 60-period series.
sibc-bank-credit-abs.direction: Volume rose ₹6.1L Cr period-on-period (₹223.9L Cr → ₹229.9L Cr).
chain: Bank credit stood at ₹229.9L Cr in September 2026, up from ₹223.9L Cr in August.
That ₹6.1L Cr addition is close to double the ₹3.1L Cr gain the book made from July (₹220.8L Cr) to August (₹223.9L Cr).
The pickup in monthly additions lines up with the level reaching a fresh high for this 60-period series.
sibc-bank-credit-abs.inference: September's ₹6.1L Cr addition is nearly double August's ₹3.1L Cr gain, keeping the book at a record level for this window.

sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.title: Bank credit grew 16.1% in FY26, up 5.1 points from FY25
sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.observation: Bank credit grew 11.0% in the year to March 2025 and 16.1% in the year to March 2026.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.direction: The full-year growth rate stepped up 5.1 points, from 11.0% in FY25 to 16.1% in FY26.
chain: Bank credit grew 11.0% in FY25 and 16.1% in FY26.
A 5.1-point step-up is a large shift for a once-a-year measure that resets only at each March year-end.
FY26 stands out as the faster lending year of the two on this annual measure.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-acceleration.inference: This 5.1-point step-up is unchanged from the last reading, since the figure is fixed at the March close — FY26 remains the clearly faster year of the two, but the reading itself won't move again until the next year-end.

sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.title: FY26 net new bank credit ₹29.6L Cr — fixed at year-end, near record
sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.observation: Banks deployed ₹29.6L Cr of net new credit in the full year to March 2026.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.direction: This figure is unchanged at ₹29.6L Cr since the March 2026 year-end close, and sits at or near the maximum of this 60-period series.
chain: The FY26 net addition stands at ₹29.6L Cr, unchanged since the March close.
As an annual figure fixed once a year, it does not move with the monthly data between year-ends.
It sits at or near the high end of this 60-period series.
sibc-bank-credit-fy-delta.inference: Because this reading is locked at the March year-end, its steady ₹29.6L Cr value says nothing about conditions since March — the monthly absolute and YoY signals carry that part of the story.

sibc-bank-credit-yoy.title: Bank credit growth rebounds to 19.38% YoY, a fresh high
sibc-bank-credit-yoy.observation: Bank credit grew 19.38% year-on-year in September 2026, at or near the highest reading in this 36-period series.
sibc-bank-credit-yoy.direction: Growth rose 0.30 points (19.08% → 19.38%), reversing a dip from July's 19.3% to August's 19.1%.
chain: YoY growth climbed to 19.38% in September, up 0.30 points from August's 19.08%.
That rebound reverses August's pullback, when growth had eased from July's 19.3% to 19.1%.
At 19.38%, growth is now at or near the maximum of this 36-period window, well above the 16.2% p75 mark.
sibc-bank-credit-yoy.inference: September's rebound to 19.38% erases August's one-month dip and puts growth back at the highest level seen in this 36-period series, well above the 16.2% upper-quartile mark.

sibc-food-credit-abs.title: Food credit falls to ₹0.96L Cr — fourth straight monthly drop
sibc-food-credit-abs.observation: Food credit outstanding fell to ₹0.96L Cr in September 2026, down from ₹1.12L Cr in August.
sibc-food-credit-abs.direction: Volume declined ₹0.16L Cr period-on-period (₹1.12L Cr → ₹0.96L Cr), the fourth consecutive monthly drop since May's peak of ₹1.37L Cr.
chain: Food credit fell to ₹0.96L Cr in September, down from ₹1.12L Cr in August.
This is the fourth straight monthly decline since the ₹1.37L Cr peak in May 2026, a cumulative fall of ₹0.41L Cr.
Despite four months of decline, the level still reads above the p75 mark for this window — the upper range.
sibc-food-credit-abs.inference: Four consecutive declines from May's ₹1.37L Cr peak have pulled food credit down by ₹0.41L Cr, yet it is still reading in the upper range of this series — the earlier run-up has not been fully unwound.

sibc-food-credit-yoy.title: Food credit YoY cools to 125.71% after August's 145.81% record
sibc-food-credit-yoy.observation: Food credit grew 125.71% year-on-year in September 2026, down from August's 145.81%.
sibc-food-credit-yoy.direction: Growth decelerated 20.10 points (145.81% → 125.71%), pulling back from last period's series-high reading.
chain: YoY growth eased to 125.71% in September, down 20.10 points from August's 145.81%.
August's 145.81% had itself been a fresh high, up from July's 107.9%.
Even after this pullback, September's 125.71% remains well above the 86.8% p75 mark for this 48-period window.
sibc-food-credit-yoy.inference: The 20.10-point pullback from August's record 145.81% is a sharp deceleration, but at 125.71% growth is still far above the 86.8% upper-quartile mark for this series — still one of the strongest readings in the window even after cooling from the peak.

sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.title: Non-food credit hits ₹229.0L Cr — fresh high, up ₹6.2L Cr
sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.observation: Non-food credit outstanding reached ₹229.0L Cr in September 2026, at or near the highest level in this 60-period series.
sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.direction: Volume rose ₹6.2L Cr period-on-period (₹222.8L Cr → ₹229.0L Cr).
chain: Non-food credit rose to ₹229.0L Cr in September, up ₹6.2L Cr from August's ₹222.8L Cr.
That keeps the book at a fresh high for this 60-period series.
Since January 2023's ₹132.9L Cr, the book has added ₹96.1L Cr.
sibc-nonfood-credit-abs.inference: September's ₹6.2L Cr addition keeps non-food credit at a fresh high of ₹229.0L Cr, extending a climb that has added ₹96.1L Cr since January 2023.

sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.title: Non-food credit FY26 net add ₹29.2L Cr — fixed at year-end
sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.observation: Banks deployed ₹29.2L Cr of net new non-food credit in the year to March 2026.
sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.direction: This figure is unchanged at ₹29.2L Cr since the March 2026 year-end close, and sits at or near the maximum for this 60-period series.
chain: The FY26 non-food net addition stands at ₹29.2L Cr, fixed since the March close.
As an annual figure, it won't change again until the next year-end lock in March 2027.
It remains at or near the high end of this 60-period series.
sibc-nonfood-credit-fy-delta.inference: Because this reading is locked at the March year-end, its steady ₹29.2L Cr value reflects FY26 as a whole rather than any recent shift — the monthly absolute reading is what moves in between.

sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.title: Non-food credit growth hits 19.15% YoY — highest in dataset
sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.observation: Non-food credit grew 19.15% year-on-year in September 2026.
sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.direction: Growth rose from 18.77% in August to 19.15% in September, a 0.38-point pickup that reverses the dip from July's 19.1%.
chain: Non-food credit grew 19.15% YoY in September 2026, up from 18.77% in August — a 0.38-point increase.
That reverses August's slip from July's 19.1%, when growth had eased for the first time in months.
At 19.15%, this reading is at or near the highest level in this 36-period series, where most history sits between 11.1% and 16.3%.
sibc-nonfood-credit-yoy.inference: After one month of easing, non-food credit growth bounced straight back to the highest level in this 36-period series, where the bulk of readings have run between 11.1% and 16.3%.

sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.title: All 4 main sectors positive for a 27th straight period
sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.observation: All four main sectors posted positive year-on-year credit growth in September 2026, with the count holding at 4 of 4.
sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.direction: Breadth held at 4 of 4 sectors, unchanged from August, extending the all-sectors-positive run to 27 straight periods since July 2024.
chain: 4 of 4 main sectors showed positive YoY growth in September 2026, unchanged from August's reading of 4.
This is the 27th consecutive period of 4-of-4 breadth, a run that has held continuously since July 2024.
Across the full 48-period series, breadth sits at or near its maximum, against the stretch through September 2022 when the count read 0.
sibc-sectors-positive-yoy-count.inference: Every main sector has now grown together for 27 straight periods, one longer than the 26-period run recorded last month — far outside anything the zero-breadth years before October 2022 showed.

sector_mix.narrative: Within Trade, both Wholesale (29.1%) and Retail (18.1%) credit are strengthening on a year-on-year basis, but the sub-sectors are converging rather than diverging — the 13.2-point gap between them last period has narrowed to 11.0 points as Retail Trade's growth accelerated faster than Wholesale's.

sibc-agriculture-share.title: Agriculture's credit share ticks up to 12.31%, still near multi-year lows
sibc-agriculture-share.observation: Agriculture's share of total bank credit was 12.31% in Sep 2026.
sibc-agriculture-share.direction: Share rose 0.08 points from 12.23% in Aug 2026 to 12.31%, staying below the 12.4% level that marks the bottom quarter of this 60-period range.
chain: Agriculture's share stood at 12.31% in Sep 2026, up 0.08 points from 12.23% in Aug 2026.
A move of that size sits within normal month-to-month noise for a share reading.
At 12.31%, the share is still below the 12.4% mark that defines the bottom quarter of readings across 60 periods.
The share has slid from 13.0% in Oct 2021 to this range, and Sep's tick-up does not reverse that longer slide.
sibc-agriculture-share.inference: At 12.31%, agriculture's share has barely moved off last period's 12.23% and stays below the 12.4% level marking the bottom quarter of this 60-period range — a small tick, not a reversal of its slide from 13.0% in Oct 2021.

sibc-agriculture-yoy.title: Agriculture credit growth climbs to 19.52%, nearing 2024's 20% peak
sibc-agriculture-yoy.observation: Agriculture credit grew 19.52% YoY in Sep 2026.
sibc-agriculture-yoy.direction: Growth accelerated 2.30 points from 17.22% in Aug 2026 to 19.52%, moving further above the 17.4% level that marks the top quarter of this range.
chain: Agriculture credit grew 19.52% YoY in Sep 2026, up 2.30 points from 17.22% in Aug 2026.
That puts growth above the 17.4% mark defining the top quarter of readings across 48 periods.
The series held at 20.0% for three straight months in Jan-Mar 2024 before falling all the way to 6.8% in Jun 2025.
At 19.52%, growth is now within half a point of that 20.0% peak after the sharp slowdown through mid-2025.
sibc-agriculture-yoy.inference: Agriculture credit growth has climbed back to 19.52%, within half a point of the 20.0% peak hit in early 2024, after falling as low as 6.8% in Jun 2025 — one of the sharper round-trips in this 48-period series.

sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.title: Industry credit grew 9.1% in FY25, 14.8% in FY26 — a 5.7-point step-up
sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.observation: Industry credit's full-year growth stepped up 5.7 points, from 9.1% in the year to Mar 2025 to 14.8% in the year to Mar 2026.
sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.direction: Full-year growth rose from 9.1% in FY25 to 14.8% in FY26, a 5.7-point step-up.
chain: Industry credit grew 9.1% in the year to Mar 2025 and 14.8% in the year to Mar 2026 — a 5.7-point step-up.
This is an annual measure fixed only at each March year-end, not a monthly trajectory.
A 5.7-point jump in full-year growth is a large year-over-year step-up for this sector.
sibc-industry-fy-acceleration.inference: Industry credit's annual growth rate jumped 5.7 points between FY25 and FY26, from 9.1% to 14.8% — a step-up fixed at the Mar 2026 year-end, not a trend to read month to month.

sibc-industry-share.title: Industry's credit share rises to 21.74%, up 0.21 points
sibc-industry-share.observation: Industry's share of total bank credit was 21.74% in Sep 2026.
sibc-industry-share.direction: Share rose 0.21 points from 21.53% in Aug 2026 to 21.74%.
chain: Industry's share stood at 21.74% in Sep 2026, up 0.21 points from 21.53% in Aug 2026.
That lifts the share back above the 21.7% mark, near the middle of this 60-period range, after touching 21.5% as recently as Aug 2026.
The share has fallen from 27.1% in Oct 2021 to this range, and Sep's uptick is a small move within that longer slide.
sibc-industry-share.inference: At 21.74%, industry's share has only just climbed back to the 21.7% mark near the middle of this range, well below the 27.1% it held in Oct 2021 — the broader slide in industry's share of the credit book continues even with this small uptick.

sibc-industry-yoy.title: Industry credit re-accelerates to 19.46% after August's dip
sibc-industry-yoy.observation: Industry credit grew 19.46% YoY in Sep 2026.
sibc-industry-yoy.direction: Growth accelerated 1.23 points from 18.23% in Aug 2026 to 19.46%, nearing the 20.0% peak hit in Jul 2026.
chain: Industry credit grew 19.46% YoY in Sep 2026, up 1.23 points from 18.23% in Aug 2026.
That rebound follows Aug's pullback from the 20.0% peak reached in Jul 2026.
At 19.46%, growth sits well above the 13.0% mark that defines the top quarter of readings across 36 periods.
sibc-industry-yoy.inference: After pulling back to 18.23% in Aug 2026 from Jul's 20.0% peak, industry credit growth has re-accelerated to 19.46% — reading as a brief pause rather than a reversal of the climb from the 5.1% low recorded in Mar 2023.

sibc-infra-yoy.title: Infrastructure credit growth hits 11.79%, strongest since late 2022
sibc-infra-yoy.observation: Infrastructure credit grew 11.79% YoY in Sep 2026.
sibc-infra-yoy.direction: Growth accelerated 1.61 points from 10.18% in Aug 2026 to 11.79%, topping the 11.6% high set in May 2026.
chain: Infrastructure credit grew 11.79% YoY in Sep 2026, up 1.61 points from 10.18% in Aug 2026.
That tops the 11.6% reached in May 2026, the previous high since growth fell to -1.3% in May 2025.
At 11.79%, growth is now the closest it has been to the 12.1% and 12.0% readings recorded in Oct and Nov 2022, near the start of this 48-period series.
sibc-infra-yoy.inference: Infrastructure credit growth at 11.79% is the strongest reading since Nov 2022's 12.0%, a sharp turnaround from the -1.3% contraction recorded as recently as May 2025.

sibc-main-acceleration.title: Services leads sector acceleration at +3.97 points; only Personal Loans cools
sibc-main-acceleration.observation: Across the four main sectors, Services' YoY growth accelerated the most this period, up 3.97 points, while Personal Loans accelerated just 0.33 points.
sibc-main-acceleration.direction: The gap between the fastest (Services, +3.97 points) and slowest (Personal Loans, +0.33 points) widened to 3.64 points.
chain: Services accelerated 3.97 points, the most of the four main sectors, while Personal Loans accelerated only 0.33 points — a 3.64-point gap.
Agriculture (+2.30 points) and Industry (+1.23 points) also strengthened, flipping from stable and weakening respectively into strengthening.
Personal Loans is the only one of the four to cool, shifting from strengthening to stable even with its +0.33-point gain.
With rotation mass of just 0.38 points, the overall sector mix barely moved even as three of the four sectors strengthened.
sibc-main-acceleration.inference: All four main sectors accelerated this period, but Personal Loans' shift from strengthening to stable — while the other three, led by Services' +3.97-point jump, all moved into strengthening — is the only cooling signal in an otherwise broad-based speed-up.

sibc-main-allocation.title: Services and Personal Loans dominate new credit allocation at up to 38.9%
sibc-main-allocation.observation: Across the readings in this scan, Services' share of new 12-month credit ranged 26.3%-38.9%, Personal Loans 28.8%-33.0%, Industry 21.4%-22.0%, and Agriculture 12.1%-12.5%, with the four sectors together capturing 94.8% of total allocation.
sibc-main-allocation.direction: Industry and Agriculture held in tight bands (21.4%-22.0% and 12.1%-12.5%), while Services and Personal Loans swung far wider (26.3%-38.9% and 28.8%-33.0%).
chain: The four main sectors together captured 94.8% of new 12-month credit allocation.
Services' share of that new credit ranged from 26.3% to 38.9% across these readings, and Personal Loans from 28.8% to 33.0% — far wider than Industry's 21.4%-22.0% or Agriculture's 12.1%-12.5%.
Rotation mass of 37.73 points reflects how much of the allocation mix moved across these readings, consistent with the wide swings in Services and Personal Loans.
sibc-main-allocation.inference: Services and Personal Loans show far more movement in their share of new credit (a 12.6-point band and a 4.2-point band) than Industry (0.6 points) or Agriculture (0.4 points), consistent with the 37.73-point rotation mass across the mix — allocation volatility is concentrated in the two largest categories, not spread evenly across all four.

sibc-main-momentum.title: Services adds ₹14.3L Cr in 12 months, most of four sectors
sibc-main-momentum.observation: Services added ₹14.32L Cr of bank credit over the last 12 months, the most of the four main sectors.
sibc-main-momentum.direction: Personal Loans added ₹10.93L Cr, Industry ₹8.11L Cr and Agriculture ₹4.60L Cr — a spread of ₹9.72L Cr between Services and Agriculture, with all four sectors strengthening.
chain: Services added ₹14.32L Cr of bank credit over the trailing 12 months, ahead of Personal Loans' ₹10.93L Cr, Industry's ₹8.11L Cr and Agriculture's ₹4.60L Cr.
The ₹9.72L Cr spread between the fastest (Services) and slowest (Agriculture) builder shows new credit concentrating in two of the four main sectors.
All four sectors are marked strengthening, so this build-up is adding on top of an already-rising base, not reversing a decline.
sibc-main-momentum.inference: Services and Personal Loans continue to account for the bulk of new bank credit among the four main sectors; Services' ₹14.32L Cr addition is ₹9.72L Cr ahead of Agriculture's ₹4.60L Cr, the full spread between the two ends of the distribution.

sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.title: Personal Loans' share dips to 32.3% as Industry, Agriculture gain
sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.observation: Personal Loans holds 32.3% of all bank credit, the largest of the four main sectors, while Agriculture holds the smallest at 12.3%.
sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.direction: Personal Loans' share has turned from strengthening to weakening (32.6% → 32.3%), while Industry (21.4% → 21.6%) and Agriculture (12.2% → 12.3%) have flipped from weakening to strengthening — a spread of 20.0 points between the top and bottom sector.
chain: Personal Loans' share of all bank credit is 32.3%, still the largest of the four main sectors but now marked weakening.
Industry (21.6%) and Agriculture (12.3%) have both flipped from weakening to strengthening this period, the first such shift in this distribution.
With three of four sectors now marked strengthening and only Personal Loans weakening, the status mix has reversed — the spread between top and bottom sector stays at 20.0 points.
sibc-main-share-of-credit-scan.inference: Personal Loans' flip to weakening at 32.3% is the only sector losing ground this period, even as it keeps the largest share of all bank credit, 20.0 points ahead of Agriculture's 12.3%.

sibc-main-share-scan.title: Personal Loans' non-food credit share falls to 32.4%, still largest
sibc-main-share-scan.observation: Personal Loans holds 32.4% of non-food credit, the largest of the four main sectors, while Agriculture holds the smallest at 12.3%.
sibc-main-share-scan.direction: Personal Loans has shifted from strengthening to weakening (32.7% → 32.4%), while Industry (21.5% → 21.7%) and Agriculture (12.2% → 12.3%) have shifted from weakening to strengthening — a spread of 20.1 points between the top and bottom sector.
chain: Personal Loans' share of non-food credit is 32.4%, the largest among the four main sectors, but has turned from strengthening to weakening this period.
Industry (21.7%) and Agriculture (12.3%) have both turned from weakening to strengthening, meaning three of the four sectors are now gaining share.
The spread between the largest and smallest share holder stays at 20.1 points even as the status mix across the four sectors has reversed.
sibc-main-share-scan.inference: Personal Loans is now the only main sector losing share of non-food credit, a reversal from when it and Services were the two gainers, while Industry and Agriculture have both turned to strengthening at 21.7% and 12.3%.

sibc-main-size-scan.title: Main-sector bank credit hits ₹217.1L Cr — highest on record
sibc-main-size-scan.observation: Bank credit to the four main sectors reached ₹217.1L Cr in Sep 2026, the highest level in this 60-period series.
sibc-main-size-scan.direction: The total rose ₹211.1L Cr → ₹217.1L Cr, up ₹6.08L Cr, and is up from ₹103.8L Cr in Oct 2021.
chain: Main-sector bank credit stands at ₹217.1L Cr in Sep 2026, up ₹6.08L Cr from ₹211.1L Cr last period.
This is the highest reading across the full 60-period series, which began at ₹103.8L Cr in Oct 2021.
A series at or near its maximum with status active means the climb is continuing rather than levelling off.
sibc-main-size-scan.inference: At ₹217.1L Cr, main-sector bank credit is at its highest point across the full 60-period series that started at ₹103.8L Cr in Oct 2021.

sibc-main-yoy-scan.title: Services YoY credit growth widens lead to 28.3%, fastest of four
sibc-main-yoy-scan.observation: Services grew 28.3% YoY, the fastest of the four main sectors, ahead of Agriculture and Industry both at 19.5%, and Personal Loans at 17.3%.
sibc-main-yoy-scan.direction: Services leads at 28.3% YoY (24.3% → 28.3%), with Agriculture and Industry now tied at 19.5% and Personal Loans slowest at 17.3% — the fastest/slowest spread has widened 7.4 → 11.1 points.
chain: Services grew 28.3% YoY, the fastest of the four main sectors, up from 24.3% last period.
Agriculture and Industry are now tied at 19.5% YoY, with Industry's status shifting from active to strengthening.
The spread between the fastest and slowest sector has widened to 11.1 points, from 7.4 points last period, as Services pulls further ahead while Personal Loans stays slowest at 17.3%.
sibc-main-yoy-scan.inference: Services, now at 28.3% YoY, is pulling further away from the other three main sectors — the fastest/slowest spread has widened from 7.4 to 11.1 points — while Industry's shift to strengthening lands it level with Agriculture at 19.5%.

sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.title: PFIs' YoY growth decelerates 4.03 points, flipping from strengthening
sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.observation: Public Financial Institutions' YoY growth rate fell 4.03 points this period, while Housing Finance Companies' rate fell 0.25 points.
sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.direction: PFIs flipped from strengthening to weakening (+4.26 → -4.03 points) while HFCs flipped from weakening to stable (-1.07 → -0.25 points).
chain: PFIs' YoY growth rate decelerated by 4.03 points this period, against HFCs' smaller 0.25-point deceleration.
This is a reversal from last period, when PFIs accelerated by 4.26 points and HFCs decelerated by 1.07 points — PFIs has now flipped from strengthening to weakening.
HFCs' deceleration eased from 1.07 points to 0.25 points, moving its status from weakening to stable, while PFIs is now the one losing pace.
sibc-nbfc-sub-acceleration.inference: PFIs' swing from a 4.26-point acceleration last period to a 4.03-point deceleration now is the sharper move of the two, flipping it to weakening just as HFCs' own deceleration eased enough to read stable.

sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.title: PFIs take up to 71.9% of new NBFC credit across nine cuts
sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.observation: Public Financial Institutions took as much as 71.9% of new NBFC credit in one reading in this distribution, while Housing Finance Companies took as little as 9.6% in another.
sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.direction: Across the nine readings, PFIs ranged 71.9% → 12.9% and HFCs ranged 28.1% → 9.6%, with the combined total reading at 33.6% in one cut.
chain: Public Financial Institutions' highest reading across the nine cuts is 71.9% of new NBFC credit, against Housing Finance Companies' highest of 28.1%.
Housing Finance Companies' lowest reading is 9.6%, narrower than Public Financial Institutions' lowest of 12.9%, giving a 62.3-point spread across all nine readings.
All nine readings are marked active, so this spread describes the current state of allocation rather than a status change.
sibc-nbfc-sub-allocation.inference: Public Financial Institutions' top reading of 71.9% remains well above Housing Finance Companies' top reading of 28.1%, continuing the wider and higher-reaching set of allocation values for Public Financial Institutions seen across these nine cuts.

sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.title: PFIs add 1.64 lakh units of NBFC credit, still ahead of HFCs
sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.observation: Public Financial Institutions added 1.64 lakh units of NBFC credit over the trailing 12 months, against 63,992 for Housing Finance Companies.
sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.direction: PFIs' 12-month addition eased slightly (1.67 lakh → 1.64 lakh units) while HFCs rose slightly (63,524 → 63,992), leaving a 99,676-unit spread between the two.
chain: Public Financial Institutions added 1.64 lakh units of NBFC credit over the trailing 12 months, against Housing Finance Companies' 63,992.
The 99,676-unit spread between the two is the full gap in this two-entity distribution, both currently marked active.
Public Financial Institutions remains the larger of the two contributors to NBFC credit's 12-month build-up, as it was last period at 1.67 lakh units.
sibc-nbfc-sub-momentum.inference: Public Financial Institutions' 1.64 lakh units added stays well ahead of Housing Finance Companies' 63,992 over the same 12 months, continuing its role as the larger contributor to NBFC credit's build-up, little changed from 1.67 lakh units last period.

sibc-nbfc-sub-share-scan.title: HFC-PFI share gap widens to 0.9 points as PFI weakens

sibc-food-processing-sub-acceleration.title: Food-processing credit swings: Others +0.63 points, Edible Oils -0.52
